subject: Request: SLA exemption for Lumen preview rollout
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Liu <emma@horizon.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, Grace Oconnor <grace@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: SLA exemption for Lumen preview rollout

Hi Emma / Jordan,

Thanks again for the productive demo yesterday. As we discussed, Horizon's integration with Lumen-Preview is scheduled to enter a limited beta on June 22. Lumen-Preview is a new model variant that improves recall on domain-specific queries but is still in our preview channel with ongoing latency optimizations.

To avoid a hard stop for your trials, we're proposing a temporary SLA exemption for the preview period. Specifically: a 60-day carveout starting June 22 where Redwood will commit to a best-effort latency target (p95 <= 450ms) and a reduced uptime SLO of 97%. In return, Redwood will:
- Provide continuous monitoring and daily telemetry summaries for the rollout window (tokens, p95/p99 latencies, error rates).
- Implement automatic safe-fallback to the stable model family when latency or error thresholds are exceeded.
- Run a joint post-mortem on any outage >30 minutes.

I've attached a short proposal (lumen_preview_sla_proposal.pdf) and the proposed rollout timeline (rollout_timeline.xlsx). Can you confirm whether Horizon can accept the temporary SLO adjustments and the fallback policy? If yes, we'll coordinate legal for a short addendum and schedule engineering handoffs.

Cc'ing Rishi (legal) and Grace (platform) to weigh in on constraints / documentation we'll need.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
vanessa@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0124

Attachments: lumen_preview_sla_proposal.pdf (application/pdf), rollout_timeline.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)

From: Emma Liu <emma@horizon.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jordan Pierce <jordan@horizon.ai>
Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 11:03:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Request: SLA exemption for Lumen preview rollout

Vanessa —

Appreciate the clear proposal and attachments. A few quick questions from our side before we sign off:
1) Can you confirm the expected failure modes that will trigger the automatic fallback to the stable model? We need to ensure our latency-sensitive pipelines (support routing) won't get unexpectedly downgraded.
2) For the 97% uptime SLO, does that apply to the single-region endpoint we will be using, or is that across Redwood's multi-region deployment?
3) Any limits on the allowed token volume under the exemption window? We plan a moderate pilot (≈ 12M tokens/day) for two weeks.

If you can provide those details, I can route the addendum to procurement. We're keen to move forward but need evidence that the fallback is deterministic and that monitoring gives us near-real-time alerts.

—Emma
Emma Liu
Platform Integrations Lead | Horizon Labs
emma@horizon.ai

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>

Date: Thu, 11 Jun 2026 09:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: SLA exemption for Lumen preview rollout

Thanks, Vanessa and Emma. Quick legal/product note on process and the fallback behavior:

- Trigger conditions for fallback: we will use a deterministic rule-set based on either (a) spike in 5xx error rate >0.5% over a 5-minute window, or (b) sustained p99 latency >1.2s over a 3-minute rolling window, OR (c) model OOM/serving failure. Those thresholds are configurable but reflect safe defaults.
- Region SLO: the proposed 97% uptime applies to the specified endpoint region (you'll be scoped to us-west-2 for the pilot). We will note that in the addendum.
- Token volume: the pilot volume (12M tokens/day) is acceptable under Dedicated capacity constraints for this beta, but if you go beyond the threshold we will automatically route excess to the stable model family to maintain SLOs. Please flag if you expect burst spikes >20% day-over-day.

Operational requirements: we need Horizon to accept read-only alerting access (PagerDuty + SAML) for the duration of the beta so joint incident response can proceed efficiently. We will provide the telemetry dashboard and two AlertBridge webhooks (one for on-call, one for engineering).

I'll prepare a short addendum draft capturing the above. Vanessa — once Horizon confirms the fallback conditions and access, legal can sign a limited addendum rather than a full SLA change.

—Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Sr. Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference
rishi@redwood.ai

Date: Fri, 12 Jun 2026 16:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: SLA exemption for Lumen preview rollout

Emma / Jordan —

Thanks for the quick turnaround. Based on Rishi and Grace's notes, Horizon's asks are all addressable. Summary of agreed points for the limited addendum:
- Effective window: 2026-06-22 to 2026-08-21 (60 days).
- SLOs during window: best-effort p95 <= 450ms; uptime target 97% (regional, us-west-2).
- Fallback: deterministic automatic fallback to the stable model when any one of the following occurs: 5xx >0.5% over 5 minutes OR p99 >1.2s over 3 minutes OR model-serving failure.
- Token volume: pilot cap 12M tokens/day; excess routed to stable model with notice.
- Monitoring & access: Redwood will provide a shared dashboard, daily telemetry reports, and read-only alert access. Joint post-mortem for any outage >30 minutes.
- Legal: short addendum to the Master Services Agreement capturing the above; no permanent SLA modifications.

Next steps: if Horizon confirms, I'll ask Legal to prepare the addendum and Product to schedule the engineering handoff (INF-2276). Once legal has a draft, Jordan and Emma — please loop procurement for signatures.

If no objections, consider this provisionally approved internally. Grace will open the engineering ticket to bake in the fallback rules and the deploy guard rails.

Thanks — looking forward to the pilot.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
vanessa@redwood.ai
